what: KE Holdings runs Beike, China's largest property transaction platform. It connects buyers and sellers through Lianjia's own agencies and a network of affiliated brokerages, and has added renovation, rental management and home services.
customers: Chinese home buyers, sellers and renters, plus the estate agents and brokerages on its platform.
money: commissions from developers on new home sales
moat: A verified listings database and a commission-sharing system that makes agents from competing brokerages cooperate on the same deal, which no Chinese rival has replicated.
risks: The Chinese property market has been weak for years
Net margin of about 3% is thin
New home sales depend on developers that are financially stressed
Chinese regulatory and geopolitical risk affects US-listed Chinese shares
opportunities: Revenue grew about 6% last year and about 15% a year over three years
Cash of about $8.3 billion against $1.9 billion of debt
Renovation and rental services grow regardless of transaction volumes
watch: Existing home transaction volume and the growth of non-transaction services.
